Backed sparse X and sparse_dataset()

Source: R/backed-sparse.R
anndata-backed-sparse.Rd

A backed_sparse is a backed_x for a CSR or CSC matrix on disk. [ accepts every R index form of a base matrix (positive, negative and logical vectors, repeated and unsorted positions, drop) and reads only the needed parts of data and indices into memory, using the cached indptr. The result is a sparse matrix in the same format as the file (dgRMatrix or lgRMatrix for CSR, dgCMatrix or lgCMatrix for CSC), or a plain vector when drop removes a dimension, as for a Matrix. Values carry the On-disk dtype record of data, as for read_h5ad(). A vector index such as x[i] has no rows and columns to select, so it reads the whole matrix. x[] is the whole matrix, as.matrix(x) its dense form and x$to_memory() the sparse matrix read as read_h5ad() reads it. x$format is "csr" or "csc", x$backend is "hdf5" and x$shape and x$dtype describe the matrix.

Arguments

x

A backed_sparse.

i, j

Row and column indices, as for a base matrix.

drop

Whether a single row or column becomes a vector.

...

Ignored.

name

The name of a field or method.

rows, cols

Sorted, unique row and column positions.

call

The call reported by errors.
